Sounds & spelling

Start here: German is read the way it is written.

Once you know about forty spellings (ei and ie, ch and sch, w, v, z, ä ö ü and the hard endings) you can read any German word aloud. Each lesson introduces five of them with words to hear them in, then drills only those five until you get each right twice in a row. Nothing is tested before it has been taught.

Vocabulary

The 2,000 words of the Deutsch Core 2000 deck, in ten steps of two hundred, so step one is the two hundred most useful words. Every noun comes with its article and plural, every verb with its main forms, and every word with an example sentence. Open any word to see how you do with it: meaning, spelling, listening, saying it and spotting it in its sentence.

Where the words in this app come from
  • Core 2000 (Review, Vocabulary): written for this app, chosen for a teenager’s first two years of German (A1 to B1). Standard German as spoken in Germany.
  • Written for this app, by an AI assistant: the Core 2000 words, phrases, situations, simulations, school and home days, readings, grammar examples and replies. They were drafted by Claude (an AI) while the app was built, and they await a native speaker. Treat all of it as good but unreviewed until a teacher has looked (Settings → Content review), and press ⚑ on anything that seems off.
  • Made while you study: nothing. The app does not generate German on the fly; every line you practise is one of the above.
  • My words: words you added yourself in the Notebook.
  • Audio: this device’s German voice. A native speaker’s recordings can be added in Settings.

Subtitle study

Load a video file and a subtitle track. Words in your deck become clickable.

How this works. Pick any video file on your machine and a matching subtitle file in SRT, VTT, or ASS format (German subtitles). Subtitles render over the video, and every word that exists in your Core 2000 deck becomes clickable for a definition, audio, and one-click queueing, even when it is inflected (spielst, gespielt and spielte all find spielen).

Lookup covers deck vocabulary only, not a full dictionary, so unknown words stay plain text. Streaming services that use DRM cannot be read by any browser page, so this works on local files.

Shadow mode. With subtitles loaded, the video can stop after every line: replay it, slow it down, record yourself and compare, then go on. The recording stays in this tab.

Credits

Core 2000 deck, phrases, situations, lessons and readings: written for Deutsch Flow by Claude, an AI assistant, in standard German as spoken in Germany, and awaiting review by a native speaker. The ⚑ button on any line and the review sheet above are for that.

Voice: this device’s German text-to-speech. Native recordings you import play instead.

Nihongo Flow: the sister app that Deutsch Flow grew out of. Progress in the two is kept apart.
